Emily — thanks for the questionnaire, joining Kim (security) and Ben (sales/legal) to make sure we cover everything. Below are concise, customer-ready responses; I’ve attached our residency SLA and an evidence checklist for deletion workflows. If you’d like a short call to walk the team through these, happy to schedule.

SUMMARY (hosted API):
- Region pinning: Yes — we support tenancy-level region binding. For hosted API customers, we can route and store request payloads and derived artifacts (e.g., embeddings) to a single AWS region in the US (us-west-2 or us-east-1) at onboarding.
- Short-term logs / runtime traces: default retention 14 days; can be reduced by request. These are used for debugging and SLO analysis only; PII is redacted where possible.
- Request/response content (customer data): default retention 90 days for analytics indexing and quality monitoring; by default this is retained encrypted at rest. Customers may request a shorter retention window (minimum configurable 7 days) or request pin-to-zero retention for sensitive tenants (see contractual addendum).
- In-memory / KV cache: ephemeral caches are kept for up to 24 hours by default to optimize latencies; caches do not persist to durable backups unless explicitly enabled by the customer.
- Backups & snapshots: automatic backups of persistent services are retained up to 180 days for disaster recovery. Backups are logically isolated per-tenant where the tenant has been pinned to a region.
- Deletion / erasure requests: operational purge timeline is 14 calendar days for primary runtime stores and indexes; backups and replicated snapshots are removed within 180 days. We commit to expunging customer-accessible records from live services within 14 days of an erasure request.

SECURITY & PROCESS HIGHLIGHTS:
- Encryption: Data at rest is encrypted with customer-aware KMS; we support customer-managed keys (CMK) on enterprise plans.
- Access control & logging: Access to raw customer content is limited to a small set of SRE/ops roles; all access is audited.
- Audit evidence: attached evidence checklist and a short SLA excerpt that we can include as an addendum to the contract.

ATTACHMENTS: Redwood_Data_Residency_SLA_v1.2.pdf, hostedapi-erase-evidence-checklist.xlsx

Next steps: if NovaFin needs a contractual clause for region-lock and a shorter retention guarantee (e.g., 30 days or immediate purge for specific tenants), we can produce a short addendum for signatures.

Emily / team — added technical detail below to supplement Karthik’s summary. I’ve called out the operational guarantees and some edge cases so your legal/security team has clear, testable statements.

TECHNICAL CLARIFICATIONS:
- Region pinning implementation: tenancy metadata includes a region attribute at provisioning. All inbound requests are routed through a tenant-specific ingress that enforces regional routing. Cross-region replication is disabled for pinned tenants unless explicitly enabled for DR; any replication is logged and subject to CMK controls.
- Data classification & retention tiers:
  * Ephemeral runtime (transient tokens, session caches): default TTL = 24 hours; no external backup.
  * Operational logs & traces: 14 days default; can be reduced to 7 days on request. Logs are retained for SLO analysis and incident investigations only.
  * Content store (customer inputs + derived outputs): retention tier default = 90 days; options: 30-day, 7-day, or immediate purge (contractual). Data in this tier is encrypted using customer CMK if requested.
  * Backups / snapshots: retained 180 days; snapshots are labeled by tenant id and region. We perform a rolling snapshot strategy which means a deletion from the live store will not instantly remove earlier snapshot copies — snapshots are retired on a 180-day schedule.
- Deletion workflow (high level):
  1) Customer requests erasure via support portal or API — ticket created and tagged with urgency.
  2) Automated job deletes tenant records from primary content stores (14-day window to allow in-flight consistency checks).
  3) Indexes and derived artifacts are rebuilt; any references are removed within the same window.
  4) Snapshot purge job queues tenant snapshot IDs for secure wipe on the next retention cycle (within 180 days).
- Evidence & attestation: we can provide audit logs showing the deletion workflow (suitable redaction available). For contractual addenda we will include the region-locking guarantee and the retention window that NovaFin chooses.

EDGE CASES / NOTES:
- If NovaFin opts for CMK and a separate VPC (Private deployment), we can shorten backup retention and provide faster deletion SLAs.
- For immediate legal holds, we support a temporary freeze of purge automation and provide an export of the locked dataset to an encrypted archive.

I’ve attached the erase evidence checklist which maps internal runbooks to each step in the deletion workflow. Happy to jump on a call to walk through the checklist with your engineers.
